replies.text:
Connect to the admin console on one pod and run `SHOW POOLS;` [1]. `cl_waiting` is the number of clients waiting for a server connection, and `sv_active` equal to the pool size means the pool is full [1].
```
kubectl -n feeds exec deploy/pgbouncer-feeds -- psql -h 127.0.0.1 -p 6432 -U pgbouncer pgbouncer
```
[1] PgBouncer (pgbouncer-feeds, pgbouncer-payouts)

A ReplicaSet's purpose is to maintain a stable set of replica Pods running at any given time [1]. To check how many replicas are available, run `kubectl get rs` [1].
[1] ReplicaSet
nvm did it by hand. `feeds_ro` row in SHOW POOLS: cl_waiting 0, sv_active 11. replicas are fine, it's only the leader pool (`feeds`)

messages.text: here. DON'T add pgbouncer pods. every pod opens its own pool per user. 4 pods x 40 x 4 users = 640 server conns against max_connections 400
it was 2 pods when that runbook was written. we went to 3 in september (PLAT-4410) and nobody redid the math. that one's on me
scaling back to 3
`kubectl -n feeds scale deploy/pgbouncer-feeds --replicas=3`
trying a lower pool on pgbouncer-feeds-7c9d5b6f4-2xq8p first

WORKAROUND, works on the first pod. on every pgbouncer-feeds pod:
```
kubectl -n feeds exec <pod> -- psql -h 127.0.0.1 -p 6432 -U pgbouncer pgbouncer -c "SET default_pool_size = 25;"
kubectl -n feeds exec <pod> -- psql -h 127.0.0.1 -p 6432 -U pgbouncer pgbouncer -c "RECONNECT feeds;"
```
3 x 25 x 4 = 300, under 400. clients queue in pgbouncer for a bit instead of getting 53300. do NOT raise it back. configmap fix after
done on all 3 pods
53300 gone from feed-builder logs. cl_waiting peaked around 400, draining now. /feed errors 11% -> 0.6%
pg-feeds-0 at 302 connections. good
patching pgbouncer-feeds-config to default_pool_size = 25 so a restart doesn't undo it. PR in a sec
